statement_record.book: For two side-by-side commutative squares: (a) if both squares are pullbacks then the outer rectangle is a pullback; (b) if the outer rectangle and the right-hand square are pullbacks, so is the left-hand square.
statement_record.intree: (a) pullback_paste: right square and left square pullbacks give the outer rectangle IsPullback (h ∘ k) m with legs p1 and q2 ∘ p2. (b) pullback_unpaste: right square a pullback, left square commuting (Hcomm), outer rectangle a pullback gives left square a pullback.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same: both directions over the apex-pinned IsPullback; the extra hypothesis Hcomm in (b) is exactly the book's data — the book poses two COMMUTATIVE squares, and as the in-tree comment notes (lines 155-159), the left square's commutativity is data the outer rectangle cannot recover, so stating it explicitly is faithful, not weaker.
